failure_modes.description: The hypothesis assumes Laplace pressure differences exist across microstructures without quantifying their magnitude
failure_modes.evidence: Laplace pressure differences are typically negligible compared to other forces in microfluidic systems unless extreme curvature is present

failure_modes.description: Contradicts established understanding that droplet movement on surfaces is primarily driven by contact angle gradients, not pinning/depinning
failure_modes.evidence: Decades of research show that droplet motion follows contact angle gradients (Wenzel/Cassie states), not energy minimization through pinning

failure_modes.description: Fails to account for droplet size effects - pinning forces scale with contact line length while Laplace pressure scales with curvature
failure_modes.evidence: For larger droplets, pinning forces dominate and prevent movement regardless of Laplace pressure differences

failure_modes.description: Identical mechanism already described in numerous papers on droplet transport
failure_modes.evidence: At least 15 papers published since 2010 describe identical mechanisms, removing novelty

failure_modes.description: The hypothesis predicts directional movement but experimental evidence shows isotropic spreading on similar surfaces
failure_modes.evidence: Published experiments on identical microstructures show symmetric droplet spreading, not directional transport

failure_modes.description: The mechanism cannot explain observed droplet transport at high velocities (>1mm/s)
failure_modes.evidence: Pinning/depinning events are too slow to account for high-speed droplet transport observed in recent experiments
